steps.content: [In the inn room]

The shackles jolt you awake. Sitting up abruptly, you're greeted by sunlight filtering through the leaves outside, its brightness so blinding as you squeeze your eyes shut. Gradually, your vision clears, and your racing heartbeat slows, as the details of reality come into focus.
It's been ages since contamination last triggered such a vivid nightmare. Did your encounter with Sheila yesterday leave that strong an impression? Something about it just feels off.
Morning birdsong drifts through the window, accompanied by the heady scent of datura blossoms, soothing your frayed nerves. Voices from outside suddenly interrupt your thoughts.

steps.speaker: Familiar Voice
steps.content: You don't need to bring me gifts every day, Alba. Save those for your sister when you'll see her in DisCity.

steps.speaker: Alba
steps.content: Oh, you still remember what I told you about my sister, Miss Vautour Bleu!

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Of course, I do. If I'd had a sibling who gets the chance to study in DisCity, I'd be just as excited as you.

steps.speaker: Alba
steps.content: So... um... when will it be my turn to go to DisCity?

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: I know how hard you've worked here, Alba. You've saved more than enough for your living expenses and the journey to DisCity. But without proper ID from your hometown, it'd be a huge risk for the caravan to sneak you in.

steps.speaker: Alba
steps.content: I get it! Really I do! I'd gladly take the risk. I've got my savings, even more!

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Oh, ma chérie, that's not what I meant. By risk, I mean a rare chance to slip past the checkpoints—an opening we have to wait for. But don't worry, your time will come.

steps.speaker: Alba
steps.content: Right, of course. I'm not in a rush... I get it. Just take some time.

You recognize Vautour Bleu's voice, the same one that haunted your dream. Yet now, though more distant, it also sounds more calm and real, undeniably patient. You rise and push open the window facing hers.
[Vautour Bleu's windowsill]
Vautour Bleu leans casually against the railing, her eyes following Alba as she walks away. Noticing your gaze, she turns to nod at you with a smile.
You seem busy today too, Miss Vautour Bleu. New deals in DisCity for the merchant caravan?
The small talk is a mere greeting, and you don't expect anything from it, but Vautour Bleu gestures toward you with her pipe.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Oh, did I wake you up?

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: You look well rested though. I take it that you slept well? I thought the little adventure in the alley yesterday might have left you a bit shaken.
Hmm? Something happened in an alley yesterday?

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: I wouldn't know. You should probably ask yourself. They say our dreams are echoes of our waking thoughts.
Unfazed by your subtle probing, Vautour Bleu fiddles with the plants on the balcony as she speaks. She seems so relaxed as if she's really just chatting about the weather with a neighbor.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Is this a habit of yours, drifting off into daydreams in broad daylight? What dream kept you dozing for so long?
I dreamed I was on the verge of uncovering the whole truth. A world where your townsfolk were safe from the looming threat of contamination, living the lives they'd always dreamed of.
It's clearly just some story you've made up, but you notice her pipe faintly trembles in her hand.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Well then... I hope your dream comes true.
A cluster of clouds blocks the sun momentarily so you can't see her true expression as she says that.

This is the same woman who lures immigrants with promises of so-called shelter and jobs, who just brushed off Alba's plea with flimsy excuses. Could she really mean what she said, for your dream to come true...?
Dreams alone won't change reality. And dreams promised by others are even less reliable.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Quite the philosopher, aren't you? I must admit I don't always catch the meaning of your words, my little neighbor.
Oh? Well then, once I've uncovered the truth myself, I'll be sure to expound everything in detail. By then, you'd better come up with some new tricks to dodge my questions.
The clouds part, and blinding sunlight floods the balcony and the town below once again. Evading your gaze, Vautour Bleu turns to face the town and draws in a deep breath.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Mmm... can you smell it? Butter and wheat. Primrose's quite the baker. I sometimes find myself craving her bread when I'm out in WhiteSands. You must be starving having just woken up. Don't miss out on some freshly bake bread.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Just head downhill to the town center. Try not to lose your way this time.
...Is this your way of giving me the green light to investigate?
Vautour Bleu says nothing. Instead, she simply raises her pipe and points at your head.
Vautour Bleu seems to be stifling a laugh. As you catch your reflection in the window, you finally notice that your hair is a complete mess from sleep, with an unruly cowlick sticking up.
And to think you've been holding this intense back-and-forth with Vautour Bleu with hair like this...
You could have just told me earlier, and not with that pipe...

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: But isn't that part of the fun of chatting across balconies? I'm not sure if you can hear my every word, but I know you can see my every move.

What is she hinting at now? As Vautour Bleu exhales a long plume of smoke, you find her intentions remain as enigmatic as ever. A small cup of tea is set on her windowsill, beneath which lies a worn, undelivered book of poetry.
N'importe où hors du monde

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: I had someone bring the tea over last night, but you'd already turned in. Such a shame, it's not quite the same when it's cold.

From across the way, Vautour Bleu watches as her lovely neighbor drapes on the cloak brought from DisCity and sets to work collecting evidence of her "misdeeds"—the same neighbor who seems to have forgotten the promise they made in that alley to have tea together.
With a slight shake of her head, Vautour Bleu tips the cup and lets the tea trickle into a flowerpot.
